Move the person out of the cold and remove wet clothing. Warm the centre of the body first: the chest, neck, head and groin. Use blankets or skin-to-skin contact. Give warm, sweet drinks only if the person is fully awake. Do not give alcohol. Do not put the person in a hot bath, as rapid rewarming can cause heart problems. sources.text: Frostbite is damage to skin and tissue caused by freezing. It most often affects the fingers, toes, nose and ears. Move the person somewhere warm before rewarming. Rewarm the affected area in warm water at 37 to 39 °C (99 to 102 °F) for 15 to 30 minutes. Do not rub the area, and do not use direct heat such as a fire or heater. Do not rewarm the area if there is a chance it will freeze again. Give pain relief such as ibuprofen if needed. Get medical help for all but the mildest cases.

sources.title: Hypothermia
sources.text: Hypothermia happens when the body's temperature falls below 35 °C (95 °F). Signs include shivering, slurred speech and confusion. Move the person out of the cold and remove wet clothing. Warm the centre of the body first: the chest, neck, head and groin. Use blankets or skin-to-skin contact. Give warm, sweet drinks only if the person is fully awake. Do not give alcohol. Do not put the person in a hot bath, as rapid rewarming can cause heart problems. Call emergency services if the temperature is below 32 °C.
